item.title: Addon: ExtraFanart Filler – Automatically fill in fanart1, fanart2, fanart3, ...
item.dc:creator: member10
item.description:
Hi All,
I created a Kodi addon that automatically populates fanart1, fanart2, etc. for Movies, TV Shows, and Movie Sets using the additional artwork URLs already scraped by Kodi.

When Kodi scrapes artwork, it (usually?) stores multiple fanart image URLs from online artwork providers. One URL is assigned to the standard fanart art type, while the remaining URLs are available as Remote Art through the "Choose Art" dialog.

This addon reads those additional fanart URLs and uses them to fill in the URLs for the fanart1, fanart2, fanart3, ...  artwork types. This allows skins and addons that support extrafanart to access the additional fanart images without requiring local artwork files.

The addon does not download artwork, scrape new images, or manage local artwork. It simply uses Remote Art URLs that Kodi has already scraped for fanart and assigns them to fanartX artwork.

More details are available on the GitHub project page: ExtraFanart Filler.
You can install the addon from the zip file at: script.extrafanart.filler.zip

item.title: Feature to hide the titles of unwatched episodes
item.dc:creator: member13
item.description:
Hi,

In Kodi, you can already hide the Movie plot, Episode plot, and Episode thumb for unwatched items (Settings / Media / Videos / Show information for unwatched items).

It should also be possible to hide Episode title, because an event in the next episode could be spoiled in the titles of subsequent episodes.

item.title: Kodi PC Game Launcher
item.dc:creator: member5
item.description:
Kodi Game Launcher
Turn Kodi into a console-style front end for your PC games. Browse your library with descriptions and artwork, press play, and the game starts.

Highlights
  • Any game, any store: Steam, Epic, GOG, emulators and standalone games. A Windows shortcut (.lnk) decides what runs.
  • Rich library: descriptions from IGDB and artwork from SteamGridDB (posters, fanart, logos and more).
  • Launch from Kodi: press play and the game starts, with a fullscreen fanart splash while it loads.
  • Automatic updates: install the repository once and Kodi keeps every addon up to date. Older versions stay available under "Versions".

How it works
  1. Organise: give each game a folder with a Play.avi and a .lnk shortcut.
  2. Scrape: the scraper adds each game to your Kodi library (as a movie) with metadata and artwork.
  3. Play: the launcher sees Play.avi, shows the splash and starts the shortcut.
Code:
Games\
  Hades\
    Play.avi
    Hades.lnk

Addons
  • IGDB + SteamGridDB Game Scraper (metadata.games.igdb): game metadata from IGDB, all artwork from SteamGridDB.
  • Game Launcher (service.gamelauncher): detects Play.avi, shows a fanart splash and launches the game's shortcut. Windows only.
  • Cinema Themes (service.cinemathemes): optional, plays theme music for your movie, show and game pages through mpv (needs a separate mpv.exe).

Requirements
  • Windows
  • Kodi 19 or newer
  • A free Twitch developer app (for IGDB metadata): https://dev.twitch.tv/console
  • A free SteamGridDB API key (for artwork): https://www.steamgriddb.com/profile/preferences/api

Install
  1. Download the repository zip: https://github.com/GoldStart5/Kodi-Game-...-1.0.1.zip
  2. In Kodi go to Add-ons > Install from zip file and select it.
  3. Go to Install from repository > Kodi Game Launcher Repository and install the addons you want.
  4. Follow the Installation Guide to add your keys and your games.

Important: enter your IGDB and SteamGridDB keys in the scraper's own Configure page (Add-ons > My add-ons > Information providers > Movie information providers > IGDB + SteamGridDB Game Scraper > Configure), not in the settings shown while you set a source's content. Keys entered there are not saved.

Use two smart playlists (Path contains / does not contain your games folder) to keep games and movies in separate lists.

Links
  • Source and downloads: https://github.com/GoldStart5/Kodi-Game-Launcher
  • Installation Guide: https://github.com/GoldStart5/Kodi-Game-...n-Guide.md
  • Troubleshooting: https://github.com/GoldStart5/Kodi-Game-...hooting.md
  • Changelog: https://github.com/GoldStart5/Kodi-Game-...ANGELOG.md

License: MIT. The addons are not affiliated with or endorsed by IGDB, Twitch or SteamGridDB.

Feedback and bug reports are welcome here or on GitHub. If something doesn't work, please post the relevant part of your kodi.log (search for service.gamelauncher or metadata.games.igdb).

item.title: service.trakt.relay
item.dc:creator: member6
item.description:
Trakt Relay 1.0.0~beta1

Trakt Relay scrobbles what you watch in Kodi to Trakt and syncs your library with it. It runs on Kodi 21 (Omega) and Kodi 22 (Piers).

Features
  • Scrobbles movies, episodes, live TV and recordings
  • Syncs your collection, watched status, ratings and playback progress, each direction switched on in the settings
  • Asks for a rating after you watch
  • Context menu to rate, add to your watchlist, start a rewatch of a show or sync your library
  • When you rewatch a show on Trakt, Kodi's watched status matches your rewatch progress (if setting is enabled)
  • Scrobbles that fail while Trakt can't be reached are sent later
  • Connect by entering a code or scanning a QR code
  • Optional OG Trakt theme with the red logo and hearts
  • Translated into 75 languages

Betas are in my repository and on GitHub: https://member6.github.io/repository.silvo/
https://github.com/member6/service.tra...y/releases

  • Settings are not imported from the Trakt add-on, so connect again and choose your sync settings
  • Don't run it next to the Trakt add-on, or everything is scrobbled and synced twice. Relay offers to disable it

Report problems with a debug log here in this thread or on GitHub: https://github.com/member6/service.trakt.relay/issues

item.title: used laptops turned HTPC , Share your build or tips and tricks
item.dc:creator: member11
item.description:
x86 is becoming more popular thanks to the breakthrough of having FEL on x86 through custom LibreELEC
but hardware is still relatively expensive.
for the same hardware I've noticed used laptops are much cheaper.
so this thread is exploring that , just from theoretical perspective (and awareness) and also practical perspective (people using them).

The hardware to match or better is GMKtek 3500U.

I found an Intel Chip that on paper fits the bill
Core I5-1235U

It has e cores, about 25% more powerful GPU. smaller node.
let me show with example
https://www.ebay.co.uk/itm/307117791029


since hinge is messed up, you can get this for £89.98, then another £10 say for Power brick

the iGPU needs dual channel to unlock iris, so say another £20 for RAM stick, you got this for £120. it's cheaper than N100 system and far better

the idea is to use this like a miniPC, Dev gave good advice and said not to bother, but still think it's fun to think about it.

we'd want to turn of the screen using some script , this will really reduce the power draw, you could also build a case for this , many around but below are a few ideas

https://www.printables.com/model/304678-...board-case



https://www.printables.com/model/1350556...-acer-58tx





there are many other good ones.

anyway why am I posting this, well because someone with a lower CPU laptop has already got it working

Dell Latitude E7320 laptop with i5 1145G7, 16GB RAM, Iris Xe
https://github.com/CroqueMr/libreelec-x86-DV/issues/70

and his thoughts about noise levels
Quote:it's dead quite, I put it on quite mode in bios, turned off hyperthreading, 4 cores enough.
So it does work, and the I5-1235U is better CPU for this and plentiful on broken used laptops (cheap)

anyway I'm just creating a thread in the hopes it will spur on some people who have the skill set and willingness to try this project on and post their results. 
maybe they found other good cheap CPU's that could work etc.
Thanks.

I'll be posting things related to this. maybe other cool "laptop motherboard case" designs for inspiration

item.title: OSD VideoResolution from SD, HD only To 480, 540, 576, 720, 1080
item.dc:creator: member7
item.description:
Hi there,

Don't know who had the brilliant idea to remove the highly relevant VideoResolutions OSD from the skin version="5.1.2"?
Anyway, here's how to get it back.
Open folder 1080p and find file IncludesVariables.xml, open the file and search for "VideoResolutionTypeVar"
Replace with below marked in red:

<variable name="VideoResolutionTypeVar">
<value condition="String.IsEqual(ListItem.VideoResolution,480) | [Window.IsActive(fullscreenvideo) + String.IsEqual(VideoPlayer.VideoResolution,480)]">480</value>
<value condition="String.IsEqual(ListItem.VideoResolution,540) | [Window.IsActive(fullscreenvideo) + String.IsEqual(VideoPlayer.VideoResolution,540)]">540</value>
<value condition="String.IsEqual(ListItem.VideoResolution,576) | [Window.IsActive(fullscreenvideo) + String.IsEqual(VideoPlayer.VideoResolution,576)]">576</value>
<value condition="String.IsEqual(ListItem.VideoResolution,720) | [Window.IsActive(fullscreenvideo) + String.IsEqual(VideoPlayer.VideoResolution,720)]">720</value>
<value condition="String.IsEqual(ListItem.VideoResolution,1080) | [Window.IsActive(fullscreenvideo) + String.IsEqual(VideoPlayer.VideoResolution,1080)]">1080</value>
<value condition="String.IsEqual(ListItem.VideoResolution,4K) | [Window.IsActive(fullscreenvideo) + String.IsEqual(VideoPlayer.VideoResolution,4K)]">4K</value>
<value condition="String.IsEqual(ListItem.VideoResolution,8K) | [Window.IsActive(fullscreenvideo) + String.IsEqual(VideoPlayer.VideoResolution,8K)]">8K</value>
<value condition="Window.IsActive(fullscreenvideo)">$INFO[VideoPlayer.VideoResolution]</value>
<value>$INFO[ListItem.VideoResolution]</value>
</variable>

And for a larger font, edit IncludesParameters.xml and search for "<control type="button" id="$PARAM[flag_id]">"

Replace with below marked in red:

        <definition>
            <control type="button" id="$PARAM[flag_id]">
                <width>$PARAM[flag_width]</width>
                <height>39</height>
                <align>$PARAM[flag_align]</align>
                <aligny>center</aligny>
                <font>font13_title</font>
                <textcolor>ffe0e0e0</textcolor>
                <textoffsetx>8</textoffsetx>
                <texturefocus border="32,2,2,2">$PARAM[flag_texture]</texturefocus>
                <texturenofocus border="32,2,2,2">$PARAM[flag_texture]</texturenofocus>
                <label>$PARAM[flag_label]</label>
                <visible>$PARAM[flag_visible]</visible>
            </control>
        </definition>

item.title: Mouse Movement triggers Kodi In-Game Menu
item.dc:creator: member9
item.description:
On Windows 11 64 bit, when I launch a PS1 game with a mouse attached (to play mouse based games such as Civ II), any mouse/cursor movement in any direction causes the game to pause and the Kodi in game menu to appear. (The menu is the Kodi one as shown here, not a menu native to the game itself). This also happens if I click the left mouse button, but not the right button. It happens with both USB and bluetooth connected mice, and with Beetle and PCSX ReARMed emulators. No other controllers or keyboards are connected at the time. It happens with Kodi v21.3 (stable) and v22 RC1 (pre-release) versions. I've set up the Playstation mouse buttons. (By the way, it also happens with LibreElect v12.2.1 on a Raspberry Pi.)

I've searched for this issue, but not seen it described elsewhere making me think (hope) it's something I've done wrong rather than a real Kodi issue. But I can't seem to figure out the cause.

(Reposted from Support > Add-on Support > Game Add-ons)

item.title: [Release] CableBox 42 – retro cable TV from your own library (Kodi 21)
item.dc:creator: member1
item.description:
Hi all,

I've made an add-on that turns your Kodi library into live cable TV. Instead of picking something to watch, you flip channels – shows are already playing on a real schedule, with commercial breaks, bumpers, a scrolling program guide channel, a retro weather channel and static between channels.

Highlights:
- Builds a channel lineup from your library automatically (genre networks, decade channels, movie channels, studio channels)
- Commercials, bumpers and station IDs from your own clip folders
- Weekly planner: pin shows to fixed times, e.g. Seinfeld every Friday at 8 PM, in order
- Off-air hours with a 1950s "Please Stand By" card, plus sign-off/sign-on clips
- Glowing "CH 03" channel numbers and an optional CRT effect (scanlines, curved glass, rolling hum bar)
- Uses Kodi's own player, so hardware decoding works as normal

It was inspired by FieldStation42 by Shane Mason (no code shared – it's a separate implementation built for Kodi).

Download and full guide: https://github.com/member1/script.cablebox42
Install: grab the zip from the Releases page and use Settings → Add-ons → Install from zip file. It's also been submitted to the official Kodi repository.

I've tested it on an ODROID N2 with CoreELEC 21. I'd love testers on other devices – Windows, Android TV / Shield / Fire TV, Raspberry Pi, LibreELEC. If something goes wrong, please post here or open an issue on GitHub with your device and Kodi version, and upload your log to https://paste.kodi.tv/ and share the link.

Thanks for taking a look!

item.title: DVD ISO Naming
item.dc:creator: member2
item.description:
I hope some can help me.  I am relatively new to Kodi and am having a problem getting two DVD ISOs to scan.  I am assuming I have the naming incorrect, but have read the wiki and a number of posts in various forums with no success.

There are two dvds each with two espisodes each of a tv mini-series.

The current naming is

item.title: Encore: Alexa voice control for Kodi, self-hosted (a successor to Kanzi)
item.dc:creator: member12
item.description:
Encore: control Kodi with Alexa, self-hosted and set up from a web interface

Since Kanzi was archived, there hasn't been a maintained way to control Kodi with an Echo, so I've built one. Encore is a self-hosted Alexa skill server for Kodi. It runs on your own network, talks to Kodi over JSON-RPC, and deploys a private Alexa skill into your own Amazon developer account, so nothing goes through anyone else's servers. A big thank you to m0ngr31 for Kanzi, which this picks up from: Encore keeps its voice commands and replaces the setup.

Say "Alexa, ask encore to play the next episode of Severance" and Alexa sends the request to Encore, which finds the episode in your library and tells the right Kodi to play it.



What's different from Kanzi
  • Set up in a web interface. A first-run wizard walks through the admin account, the public address, Kodi, your Amazon developer account and the first deploy. No hand-made skill in the developer console, no pasting interaction models, no Lambda or Heroku.
  • One-click skill deploys. Encore builds the skill and creates or updates it in your developer account through Amazon's Skill Management API.
  • Your library in the skill. Titles, rooms and playlists become slot values when you deploy, so Alexa recognises the names you actually have, and Encore's own matcher finds the ones that don't fit ("rocky two", "endgame", titles Alexa has never heard of). When two titles are close, it asks which one you meant.
  • New titles are findable straight away. Kodi's live notifications keep Encore's index of your library up to date, so something added a minute ago can be played by voice without a redeploy.
  • Rooms and several Kodi instances. Link each Echo to a Kodi instance, or name a room: "play Dune in the bedroom". Instances sharing a MySQL/MariaDB library are detected automatically.
  • Wake-on-LAN. A sleeping Kodi is woken and the request retried.
  • A live request log and match tester. See what Alexa heard, how it was matched, which Kodi calls were made and how long each step took.
  • Nine locales in five languages: English (Australia, Canada, India, United Kingdom, United States), German, French, Spanish and Italian.

What you can say
Everything Kanzi understood, and a few more:
  • Play a movie, a specific episode ("season 4 episode 10 of The Office"), the next or newest episode of a show, or continue the last show you watched
  • Play or shuffle music by song, album, artist or genre, music videos, and audio and video playlists, including smart playlists
  • Random movies, episodes and shows, by genre too, and recommendations with a follow-up ("want to see the trailer?")
  • Playback control: play/pause, stop, skip, seek ("go to the 20 minute mark"), shuffle and repeat
  • Volume, mute, subtitles and audio tracks
  • Navigate Kodi like a remote: up, down, select, back, menus, library views; the skill stays open, so you don't repeat the wake word
  • "What's playing?", "how long is left?", "when does this finish?" and "what's new?"
  • Open add-ons, search everything (with Global Search), update or clean the library
  • Shut down, reboot, sleep or hibernate, with a confirmation first
The full list of phrases for each language is in the voice commands reference.

Screenshots
Kodi instances, with discovery, connection and library details:


Deploying the Alexa skill, with the model for each locale:


The live request log:


The library index and match tester:


Echo devices and rooms:


There's a tour of the whole web interface in the docs.

What you need
  • Kodi 21 (Omega) or 22 (Piers) with Allow remote control via HTTP and Allow remote control from applications on other systems turned on (Settings → Services → Control). See Kodi instances.
  • A free Amazon developer account, the same Amazon account your Echo uses. The skill stays private to your account and never needs certifying. See deploying the skill.
  • A public HTTPS address for Alexa to reach. Only one route, /api/v1/alexa, has to be exposed, through a reverse proxy (Caddy, Traefik, SWAG, nginx) or a tunnel (Cloudflare Tunnel, Tailscale Funnel). See exposing Encore to Alexa.
  • Somewhere to run it: a container image for amd64, arm64 and armv7 (Raspberry Pi), or a single binary for Linux, macOS and Windows.

Getting started
 
Code:
docker run -d --name encore \
  -e PUID=1000 -e PGID=1000 \
  -p 8080:8080 \
  -v /path/to/encore:/config \
  ghcr.io/member12/encore
Then open http://<your-server>:8080, paste the setup token from the log and follow the wizard. The docs cover each step:
  • Why Encore: what it is and how it fits together
  • Running with Docker or as a binary
  • First run: the setup wizard, step by step
  • Echo devices and rooms
  • Matching and aliases: how titles are found, and teaching it nicknames
  • Shared libraries for MySQL/MariaDB setups
  • Storage and backups

Status
This is the first release, v0.1.0, so expect rough edges until 1.0. Voice control, the web interface and skill deploys work end to end with a real Echo, tested in English (Australia). The other locales haven't been tried on real devices yet, so if you speak German, French, Spanish or Italian, or use another English locale, I'd love to hear how it goes. Translations are on Crowdin if you'd like to improve them.

Questions are welcome here; bugs and feature requests are best as GitHub issues, with the request log entry for the command that went wrong.

Links: GitHub · Documentation · Releases · Container image

Encore is open source (Apache-2.0). Donations for this tool gratefully accepted.
